title: How does Steve get upstairs?
_story: Steve can't jump up to the next floor. A real builder measures the height, splits it into equal steps, cuts stringers, adds treads, risers and a handrail. Steve climbs it, then trips on a step that's taller than the rest.
_stepChain: too high to jump → measure floor to floor (240 cm) → equal steps of 20 → count in 20s: 12 steps → why not giant steps? (UK homes: at most 22 cm) → stringers → treads + risers → handrail + balusters → climb → one odd step: trip → every step the same

talk.ask: Why must every step be the same height?
talk.goodAnswer: your legs get used to the height after a step or two; a step that's different catches your foot and you trip.

talk.ask: How do builders work out how many steps?
talk.goodAnswer: measure the height from floor to floor, then share it into equal steps that aren't too tall, like 240 centimetres into 12 steps of 20.

handsOn: With a grown-up, measure one step of your stairs with a ruler. How tall is it? Count the steps, then count up in that number to find how high your upstairs floor is.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: I want to get upstairs, but it's far too high to jump. In my world I'd pile up blocks. How do builders make real stairs?
First the builder measures from this floor to the floor upstairs. Here it's 240 centimetres. That's taller than a grown-up.
The builder wants every step to be 20 centimetres tall.

question.prompt: Count up in twenties to 240. How many steps?

0.say: 10 steps of 20 is only 200. Two more steps reach 240: 12 steps.

2.mistake: counted in tens instead of twenties

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Why not make 4 giant steps instead? That's less work!

question.prompt: Why don't builders make giant steps?
choices: Our legs can't step that high safely
question.onRight: Yes. In homes in the UK, each step can be at most 22 centimetres tall, so legs can reach it safely.

1.mistake: thinks it's about the amount of wood
1.hint: Imagine climbing a step as high as your tummy.
1.say: It's about our legs. A step as high as your tummy is hard to climb and easy to fall from. In UK homes, each step is at most 22 centimetres.

2.mistake: thinks there's a fixed number of steps
2.hint: Do taller houses have more steps?
2.say: Stairs can have any number of steps. The rule is that each step mustn't be too tall: at most 22 centimetres in UK homes.

question.reveal: Steps must be low enough for legs: at most 22 centimetres in UK homes.

narration.text: The builder cuts two long boards with a zig-zag edge. They hold the steps up, like the sides of a ladder. They're called stringers.
Then the parts you stand on go across, one for each step. They're called treads. Between them go upright boards called risers, all exactly 20 centimetres tall.
Last comes a handrail to hold on to, on thin posts, so nobody falls off the side.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Up I go! Every step is the same height, so after one or two steps my legs know exactly what to do.
Now watch. What if one step is taller than the rest?

choices: One step was taller than the others
question.onRight: Yes. His legs expected 20 centimetres, but that step was taller, so his foot caught it.

1.mistake: blames speed instead of the odd step
1.hint: Watch which step he tripped on. Is it the same as the others?
1.say: He climbed at the same speed as before. This time one step was taller, so his foot caught its edge.

2.hint: He climbed the same long stairs before without tripping. What changed?
2.say: The stairs are as long as before. What changed is one step: it's taller than the others, and his foot caught it.

question.reveal: One step was taller, so his foot caught it. That's why every step must be the same.

rule.text: Measure the height, then make every step the same.
rule.ask: Can you say how stairs are made? Say it out loud. Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: Measure from floor to floor, share it into equal steps that aren't too tall, then build: stringers, treads, risers and a handrail.

bonus.prompt: Bonus: each step is 20 centimetres. How high are 5 steps?

0.hint: Each of the 5 steps is 20 tall. Count in twenties.
0.say: You added 20 and 5. Count 20 for each step: 20, 40, 60, 80, 100.

2.say: 50 would be 5 steps of 10. In twenties it's 100.
